findings.title: OAuth flow with per-user page picker
findings.detail: Users go to the authorization URL, choose pages in the page picker, and Notion redirects with a code. The app exchanges the code for an access_token and refresh_token at the token endpoint. Each user must authorize individually. Authorization can start once client credentials and a redirect URI are configured; Marketplace review is not required.

evidence.quote: Both scoped OAuth integrations and public integrations use this flow. You can start authorization as soon as you configure the integration’s client credentials and redirect URI; Marketplace submission or review

findings.appliesWhen: Reading titles and content of shared pages

steps.title: Create a public OAuth connection in the Developer portal
steps.detail: Open the Developer portal at https://app.notion.com/developers/connections (Build > Connections > Create new connection). Enter the connection name, development workspace and redirect URI(s). Choose installation scope 'Any workspace', because customer workspaces must be able to install it; scope cannot be changed after creation. Select only the 'Read content' capability. Do not select Update or Insert content.
steps.doneWhen: The connection exists with 'Any workspace' scope, a registered redirect URI and only the Read content capability checked.

evidence.quote: Fill out the form with your connection details, including your redirect URI(s) under the OAuth configuration section and the connection's installation scope — either **Any workspace** or **Or select 1

Select **Create new connection**. Enter the connection name, development workspace, and redirect URIs. Choose **Or select 1 or more workspaces**, select the workspaces, and choose the capabilities your app needs.
* **Read content**: This capability gives a connection access to read existing content in a Notion workspace. For example, a connection with only this capability is able to call Retrieve

steps.title: Collect client credentials and authorization URL
steps.detail: Open the connection's Configuration tab and copy the OAuth client ID, OAuth client secret and authorization URL. Store them in environment variables or a secret manager (e.g. OAUTH_CLIENT_ID, OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET, NOTION_AUTH_URL). Never commit them to source code or version control.
steps.doneWhen: Client ID, client secret and authorization URL are available to the server only through environment variables or a secret manager.

steps.title: Implement the server callback at the redirect URI
steps.detail: The agent can draft the handler; the developer implements it. The callback route must match a registered redirect URI. It should read the code and state query parameters, verify state against the value stored for the initiating session (state is optional in the docs but supports CSRF protection), and handle error=access_denied when the user cancels. The docs describe no PKCE or account-choice parameter, so none is required. Keep token exchange server-side.
steps.doneWhen: The callback route is reachable over HTTPS at the registered URI, parses code, state and error, and rejects a mismatched state.

steps.title: Exchange the code for tokens on the server
steps.detail: The developer runs a server-side POST to the token endpoint using HTTP Basic auth (base64 of CLIENT_ID:CLIENT_SECRET) and a JSON body with grant_type=authorization_code, code, and redirect_uri (required when supplied in the authorization URL or when multiple redirect URIs are registered). Response includes access_token, refresh_token, bot_id, owner, workspace_id and workspace_name.
steps.doneWhen: The response contains access_token, refresh_token, bot_id and workspace_id for the authorizing user.

evidence.quote: Next, send the `code` as part of a `POST` request to Notion’s token endpoint: https://api.notion.com/v1/oauth/token.
The request is authorized using HTTP Basic Authentication. The credential is a colon-delimited combination of the connection’s `CLIENT_ID` and `CLIENT_SECRET`, like so:
| `"grant_type"` | `string` | Always use `"authorization_code"`. | ✅ |

steps.title: Store tokens bound to user and workspace
steps.detail: Persist access_token and refresh_token together with bot_id, workspace_id and the owner user from the response, keyed so each user's grant in each workspace is stored separately and one person's authorization never overwrites or is reused by another. Store all returned fields, encrypt tokens at rest, never log them, and replace the pair on re-authorization.
steps.doneWhen: Two test users in one workspace each have distinct stored token records keyed by user and workspace_id; neither overwrote the other.

steps.title: Implement token refresh
steps.detail: Send a server-side POST to the token endpoint with Basic auth and grant_type=refresh_token plus the stored refresh_token. A new access_token and new refresh_token are returned; replace both stored values for that same user and workspace.
steps.doneWhen: A refresh returns a new token pair that replaces the stored pair for the correct user and workspace.
